title: Perioperative sonographic examinations in plastic and reconstructive surgery
summary:
It is of great interest to our clinic to learn how we can use ultrasound examinations to increase safety before and during operations  and improve preoperative planning.   
Ultrasound examinations enable us to gain essential insights into the blood vessels supplying the tissue that is being treated  is used, for example, to reconstruct the patient's own breast (e.g. DIEP/msTRAM) or to repair wounds, known as skin/soft tissue defects. 
An examination lasting approximately 20-30 minutes is planned as part of the preparation for surgery. During this examination, relevant anatomical structures in the surgical area are visualised using ultrasound. Ultrasound examination is a safe, widely used method that is non-invasive and does not involve any other risks. Patients will not derive any individual health benefits from participating in this study. However, the results of the study may help other people in the future by reducing radiation exposure during other preliminary examinations (e.g. computed tomography).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria are patients over the age of 18 with planned autologous breast reconstruction using DIEP/msTRAM flap plasty.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria include patients who have undergone non-minimally invasive abdominal surgery and patients under the age of 18.
